claim: Iter125 SHARP STRUCTURAL FALSIFICATION of the saturation model + three-phase hypothesis. (1) Monotonicity is rejected for ALL 5/5 anchors: per-pair violation rate 0.29-0.46, far above the i.i.d. 5% noise floor (each anchor's binom p < 0.001, majority-violate binomial p = 0.0312). The saturation model R(t)=R_max*(1-exp(-lambda*t)) implies strict monotonicity, so the model is misspecified by construction. (2) Three-phase hypothesis (arXiv 2507.18014) FALSIFIED: only 1/5 (Qwen3-8B, which is monotone-plateau-collapse) exhibits all three phase signatures; the dominant signature is collapse_only (4/5) or monotone_or_plateau (3/5). Phase1 (improvement) appears in only 1/5 anchors. (3) Residual decomposition: for the 3 capable anchors, structural_share of saturation residuals is 81-88%, confirming the misspecification is structural (segment-mean deviation), not i.i.d. noise. (4) R_max bimodality: 5 R_max values split cleanly at the largest gap of 0.5313 into incapable (0.182, 0.285) and capable (0.817, 0.844, 0.869) clusters, Hartigan dip=0.522, bootstrap p=0.056. Conclusion: scale has weak leverage on GRPO reward trajectory; the dominant axis is capability-class (instruct/base + collapse risk), not parameter count. The 'no scaling law' verdict from iter117/iter121 is now sharpened from 'silent evidence base' to 'wrong model class'.

Iter126 ZVF TRAJECTORY DYNAMICS elevate ZVF from a static cross-library diagnostic (iter118/iter122) to a dynamical EWS for GRPO collapse, with three falsifiable findings on the variance-mitigation suite (9 methods x 5 seeds). H1 (Critical Slowing Down): GRPO-collapse seeds (n=3) have rolling lag-1 autocorrelation 0.609 +/- 0.036 (window=15) on the pre-event ZVF trajectory, vs GRPO-safe seeds (n=2) 0.415 +/- 0.008; Cohen's d = 7.3 (very large). The single integrated lag-1 statistic over the same window is non-discriminating (0.992 vs 0.993, d=-0.37), confirming the rolling-window EWS statistic is what carries the critical-slowing-down signal (Scheffer 2009). H2 (Threshold-crossing lead time): For each tau in {0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7} the first ZVF >= tau crossing is STRICTLY BEFORE the GRPO collapse onset in all 3 collapse seeds, with minimum lead time 19 steps (tau=0.7, seed=0) and maximum 39 steps (tau=0.4, seed=2). Mean lead times: 35.7, 32.3, 28.7, 24.3 for the four thresholds. All 12 lead times are non-negative -- ZVF is a LEADING indicator of GRPO collapse in the iter118 high-ZVF calibration band. H3 (ZVF drift slope as method-level discriminator): GRPO first-half ZVF slope is 9.91e-3/step, 24x AERO (0.41e-3), 5-6x NGRPO/SCAFGRPO/CPPO, ~100x AREAL (-0.00e-3). The slope order matches the iter118 mean-ZVF order (Spearman rho=1.0 across 9 methods), but the quantitative gap (24x) explains structurally why AERO suppresses the iter78 collapse EWS: it pushes ZVF into a regime where collapse trajectories cannot develop. Practical implication: iter122's two-threshold alarm can be sharpened by adding a third channel -- rolling lag-1 > 0.55 -- that fires on the GRPO-collapse signature without false-positiveing on AERO plateau (rolling lag-1 0.24-0.51) or AREAL/GIFT drift (rolling lag-1 0.33-0.45).

Joint acc(G,T) fit: log10(1-acc)=+1.669-0.141*log10(G)-0.293*log10(T), R^2=0.796, n=20; both b (p=0.026) and c (p<1e-6) significant and negative; b/c ratio=0.48, so compute dominates group size by 2x per decade
G*(T) optimal-G-per-budget slope = +0.500/decade of T pre-saturation (G*(1M)=8, G*(4M)=16, G*(16M)=32, G*(64M)=32 -- saturated)
Bounded cone supported: acc(G=64) <= acc(G=32) at all 4/4 budgets (deltas -0.07/-0.08/-0.04/-0.01); G=32 is the high-water mark on Qwen2.5-0.5B arithmetic

Two-way compute-group complementarity: value-of-T (1M->64M) increases with G (Spearman rho=+1.0, n=5); value-of-G (4->32) increases with log T (Spearman rho=+1.0, n=4); amplification 24.0x -- compute unlocks G AND G unlocks compute

Iter130 UNIFIED ZVF RISK INDEX: elevates ZVF from single-axis static diagnostic (iter118) + trajectory-dynamics EWS (iter126) to a three-channel real-time risk score. Channels: (1) magnitude = logistic(mean_zvf, anchor=0.30); (2) CSD = logistic(rolling lag-1 of per-step ZVF, w=15, anchor=0.45, Scheffer-2009 EWS); (3) drift = logistic(first-half ZVF slope, anchor=0.004/step). Composite zvf_risk = 0.3*magnitude + 0.5*CSD + 0.2*drift; max-fusion zvf_risk_max = max(magnitude, CSD, drift). KEY RESULT: max-fusion dominates every single channel and the weighted composite. Cross-experiment AUROC (n=52: 45 variance_mitigation seeds + 2 tool_use + 5 scaling_law): zvf_risk_max=0.929 [0.83, 1.00] vs CSD alone=0.758 [0.52, 0.94] vs magnitude alone=0.663 [0.37, 0.93] vs weighted=0.763 [0.57, 0.94]. Within-method AUROC (n=45): zvf_risk_max=0.805 [0.62, 0.95] vs CSD alone=0.335 [0.11, 0.57] vs magnitude alone=0.073 [0.00, 0.26]. The 95% CI excludes 0.5 on both panels. METHODOLOGICAL INSIGHT: magnitude is anti-discriminating within methods (AUROC 0.07) because GIFT/AREAL/ES fail by going to ZERO contrast while GRPO fails by saturating contrast -- they look opposite in the magnitude channel. The max-fusion (logical-OR) is robust because the three failure modes (GRPO-style collapse, tool-use perfect-zero collapse, scaling-law collapse-phase) each surface in DIFFERENT channels but never in none. Method-level ranking (max-fusion): scaling_law_anchors 0.69 > tool_use_anchors 0.55 > GRPO 0.53 > NGRPO/CPPO/AERO 0.43-0.49 > SCAFGRPO 0.21 > GIFT/AREAL/ES 0.13-0.20. GRPO is correctly ranked ABOVE every other variance-mitigation method even though it doesn't collapse -- because its high-CSD + high-drift profile is the closest cousin of the collapse anchors. Practical threshold: zvf_risk_max > 0.55 is failure-positive, < 0.30 is safe, [0.30, 0.55] is investigate.

Iter137 THREE-PARAMETER OFFSET SATURATION FIT closes the iter117 R(0)=0 artefact. The canonical iter117 fit R(t)=R_max*(1-exp(-lambda*t)) forces R(0)=0, anchoring lambda at the upper bound (10.0) on 4/5 anchors and making the t_80-vs-N regression degenerate. Iter137 fits R(t)=c+(R_max-c)*(1-exp(-lambda*t)) with three interpretable parameters (baseline c, ceiling R_max, learning rate lambda). Result: lambda is un-bound on all 5/5 anchors (vs 4/5 anchored before), but the 3-param LOSES to 2-param by AICc on 5/5 anchors (delta_AICc +1.71 to +18.18) -- the offset parameter is not justified by the residual drop because trace variance is high. HONEST NULL: cross-scale slope on t_80 is +0.507+/-0.718 (SE, t=0.71, p>0.5); on R_max is -0.172+/-0.198 (Spearman rho=-0.658, p=0.227, n=5); on lambda is +0.063+/-0.248. Capability axis preserved: 3/2 capable/incapable split identical to iter133. Mann-Whitney U on 3-param R_max U=3.0 (p=1.0 degenerate at n=5); within-class Spearman rho non-significant at n=3. Sharpest finding: GRPO saturation is real (capable R_max>0.8, incapable R_max<0.3) but t_80, lambda, R_max do not scale with N on this evidence base even when the R(0)=0 boundary-condition artefact is removed. The cross-scale law is absent in TWO model classes (2-param and 3-param), not one.
